title: Copper Observatory
currencyNote: Original quoted currencies are preserved; no FX conversion is applied.

argus.label: Argus · reported by Reuters
argus.note: Reuters attributes the spot treatment charge to Argus. The observation is dated November 6; it is not a November 25 quote.

argusMethod.label: Argus methodology
argusMethod.note: Argus specifies RC in US cents/lb at 10% of the numerical TC in US dollars/t. The displayed RC is calculated, not independently retrieved.

platts.label: S&P Global · Platts
platts.note: CIF China clean copper concentrate TC of −$235/mt and RC of −23.5 US cents/lb, assessed October 8. Separate methodology from Argus.

acid.label: SMM · sulphuric acid review
acid.note: China copper-smelting acid index, CNY per metric tonne. Includes November 6 and the prior Friday comparison.

acidSep.label: SMM · September 18 review
acidSep.note: Copper-smelting acid index of CNY 1,351/t; previous Friday CNY 1,418/t.

acidSep30.label: SMM · September 30 review
acidSep30.note: Copper-smelting acid index of CNY 1,218.5/t; previous Friday CNY 1,247.5/t.

production.label: SMM · October output
production.note: SMM survey reports October cathode output of 1.0867 million tonnes, −3.03% MoM and −0.45% YoY. November 1.0821 Mt is a forecast and is excluded from actuals.

nbs.label: NBS · reported via SMM / Wenhua
nbs.note: Reports NBS October refined copper output of 1.2220 million tonnes, +1.80% YoY. January–October total: 12.5040 Mt, +2.70% YoY. Underlying NBS table was not retrieved directly.

customs.label: GACC · reported via SMM / Wenhua
customs.note: Customs preliminary October copper ore and concentrate imports: 216.70 ten-thousand tonnes = 2,167,000 tonnes. January–October: 24.1421 Mt, −3.80% YoY. This is gross ore/concentrate mass, not contained copper.

inventory.label: SHFE · displayed by SMM
inventory.note: SMM's exchange inventory panel displays copper inventory of 30,846 tonnes, +3,204 tonnes (+11.59%). Week-ending date is corroborated by the November 20 SP Angel report.

inventoryDate.label: SP Angel · November 20 report
inventoryDate.note: Dates SHFE weekly copper inventory of 30,846 tonnes and increase of 3,204 tonnes to the week ending November 20. Prior week value of 27,642 is calculated as 30,846 − 3,204.

shfe.label: SHFE · official weekly reports
shfe.note: Official SHFE reporting portal. Dynamic inventory table could not be extracted; displayed observations were verified through attributed public reports.

premium.label: SMM · November 25 Yangshan
premium.note: Daily Yangshan registered-copper warrant premium: $340/t, range $280–400/t, −$50/t day on day. Warrant basis is used consistently; B/L and EQ assessments are separate.

weeklyOct29.label: SMM · October 29 weekly review
weeklyOct29.note: Published review for October 26–29: average warrant premium $193/t; B/L $180/t.

weeklyNov5.label: SMM · November 5 weekly review
weeklyNov5.note: Published review for November 2–5: average warrant premium $204/t; B/L $194/t.

weeklyNov12.label: SMM · November 12 weekly review
weeklyNov12.note: Published review for November 9–12: average warrant premium $233/t; B/L $223/t.

weeklyNov19.label: SMM · November 19 weekly review
weeklyNov19.note: Review published November 19 describes November 16–20: average warrant premium $375/t; B/L $340/t. Treated as a published week-to-date assessment, not a finalized full-week average.

regimeIEA.label: IEA · the changing economics of copper smelting
regimeIEA.note: Documents negative spot TC/RCs since 2024 and a zero annual benchmark for 2026. Describes the growing role of by-products, differences between integrated and custom smelters, and the supply/capacity adjustment needed for fees to recover.

regimeIvanhoe.label: Ivanhoe Mines · Q3 2026 operating results
regimeIvanhoe.note: Kamoa-Kakula's Q3 smelter operating cost was $0.51/lb of payable copper; acid by-product credits were $0.69/lb. These are selected C1 cash-cost components on a 100% project basis, not total costs or an accounting profit margin. DRC operations do not establish Chinese smelter economics.

regimeCapstone.label: Capstone Copper · Q3 2026 operating results
regimeCapstone.note: Mantos Blancos acid prices were $316/t versus $186/t a year earlier. Mantoverde reduced acid-intensive heap throughput. Cathode output for the company's cathode business fell 48% YoY, with multiple drivers; it is not a China-wide statistic.

regimeBoliden.label: Boliden · Q3 2026 interim report, page 10
regimeBoliden.note: Boliden reported that stronger metal and acid prices offset lower treatment charges. Its Smelters segment includes copper, nickel, zinc and lead operations, so the segment result cannot be treated as a pure copper-smelting margin.

metrics.name: Spot concentrate TC / RC
metrics.meaning: Treatment and refining charges measure the fees for turning concentrate into refined copper. Negative charges mean the smelter pays for feedstock processing access.
metrics.method: Argus spot TC reported by Reuters. RC of −24.72 US¢/lb is derived using Argus's numerical 10% convention. The latest licensed assessment has not been connected.
metrics.detail: CIF China clean concentrate. TC is per dry metric tonne of concentrate; RC is per pound of payable copper. Do not compare the two units directly.

metrics.name: Chinese sulphuric acid
metrics.summary: By-product prices eased in the latest public quote.
metrics.meaning: Sulphuric acid is a key by-product of copper smelting. Its sale can support smelter economics when concentrate processing fees are weak.
metrics.method: SMM China copper-smelting acid index. This is a smelter-acid benchmark, not a universal quote for every grade or Chinese region. A newer public review exists without a retrievable numerical index.
metrics.detail: Quoted in Chinese yuan per metric tonne. The older observation is retained because the newer index value could not be verified publicly.

metrics.name: Chinese refined production
metrics.summary: October output differs across the two datasets.
metrics.meaning: Refined production tracks China's domestic copper cathode supply. SMM's survey and NBS statistics have different coverage and methods, so their totals are displayed separately.
metrics.method: SMM: 1.0867 Mt (−3.03% MoM; −0.45% YoY). NBS via Wenhua/SMM: 1.2220 Mt (+1.80% YoY). Do not splice these into a single historical series.
metrics.detail: October 2026 actuals only. The SMM November forecast is excluded. No month-on-month change is inferred for the NBS series.

metrics.name: Copper concentrate imports
metrics.meaning: Customs copper ore and concentrate imports measure feedstock entering China. This is gross imported material, not tonnes of contained or refined copper.
metrics.method: General Administration of Customs preliminary statistics, reported by Wenhua and republished by SMM on November 10. October: 2.1670 Mt. January–October: 24.1421 Mt, −3.80% YoY.
metrics.detail: Source units are 10,000 tonnes; 216.70 × 10,000 = 2,167,000 tonnes. The year-to-date change does not describe October's individual year-on-year change.

metrics.name: Shanghai copper inventories
metrics.summary: Exchange stocks rose from a low base.
metrics.meaning: SHFE copper inventory measures stocks in exchange-designated warehouses across its delivery network. It is not all copper physically stored in Shanghai and is separate from daily registered warrants.
metrics.method: SHFE data displayed by SMM; week-ending date corroborated by SP Angel. November 13's 27,642 t is calculated from 30,846 − 3,204. Weekly increase is 11.59%.
metrics.detail: Use total weekly warehouse inventory rather than daily warrant tonnage. Bonded and broader social inventories are separate datasets.

metrics.name: Yangshan cathode premium
metrics.summary: Warrant premiums pulled back on November 25.
metrics.meaning: The Yangshan premium measures the premium for imported cathode on a specified delivery basis. It is a signal of physical import appetite and availability, rather than the outright copper price.
metrics.method: SMM registered-copper warrant premium, daily average. November 25: $340/t, assessed range $280–400/t. Bills of lading and EQ cathode use separate assessments.
metrics.detail: Daily assessments and published weekly averages are separate chart views. Weekly points use publication dates; November 19 is a week-to-date publication.

regime.summary: The reversal is real. The opportunity depends on who captures the value.
regime.timing: This shift developed over 2024–26. It is not a newly verified overnight event.

exposures.mechanism: A smaller or negative processing deduction can improve concentrate sale proceeds.
exposures.verify: Check spot versus annual contracts, payability, mine costs and disruptions.

exposures.mechanism: Acid and recovered metals can offset weak processing fees. The result is plant- and region-specific.
exposures.verify: Check net acid proceeds, recovery rates, transport costs and access to buyers.

exposures.mechanism: Buying concentrate at negative fees compresses the processing revenue line.
exposures.verify: Check full margins, hedges, subsidies, premium income and actual curtailments.

exposures.mechanism: Higher purchased acid prices can raise costs or make some ore uneconomic to process.
exposures.verify: Check acid consumption, supply contracts and protection from owned smelters.
